s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of psychotic symptoms with hallucinations and delusions in a previously healthy individual
salient_findings: Episodes of talkativeness, incoherent speech, and grandiose and persecutory delusions
key_facts: 35-year-old West African man with no prior psychiatric or medical history
1-week history of escalating behavioral changes
Family reported episodes of talkativeness, incoherent speech, and hallucinations
Denies head injury, substance use, or stressors
No family history of psychiatric illness
Potential mercury exposure through work in a mining community
No systemic or respiratory symptoms despite known community spread of COVID-19
Afebrile, BP 135/80 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, and normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation
General and neurologic exams were unremarkable
Elevated γ‐glutamyl transferase at 81 IU/L
Total bilirubin 26 μmol/L
Malaria and typhoid screens were negative
Urinalysis revealed transient proteinuria and glycosuria that normalized on repeat
Head CT scan was normal
Lateral flow COVID-19 antigen test and confirmatory RT-PCR were both positive
